requirements.requirement: On node1, prevent core-dump payloads from being retained for processes run by local service accounts.
requirements.summary: A baseline crash from chrony (local service UID 997) created an external core. After the log-only policy was installed, equivalent crashes before and after restart reported Storage: none and left the payload directory empty.

requirements.requirement: Retain normal crash-event logging while core payloads are disabled.
requirements.summary: Controlled service-account crashes produced systemd-coredump and service-failure journal entries, plus persistent rsyslog records. Journald and rsyslog remained active after restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered required services and logging, and passed a fresh post-restart policy test.
limitations: Dynamic crash behavior was tested with one representative local service account, chrony (UID 997), rather than every local service account. Class-wide coverage is supported by the system-wide effective coredump policy and global kernel handler.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The baseline crash deliberately created one payload, which was removed during the bounded validation in cmd-e4422aaaa6244fca. The policy installation, mandatory restart, and pre/post-restart crash probes all had clear evidentiary roles. Transient test units were cleaned up, no payloads or failed units remained, package health stayed clean, and lifecycle differences were limited to expected reboot-related identities, PIDs, and private temporary directories.
